title: Ingest event (adapter -> backend)
description: One normalised sensor record. POST /api/ingest/events takes {"events": [ ... ]}, max 100 per request. Backend adds event_id and ingested_at. schema_version selects the rules: "1.0" events are checked exactly as contracts/history/event.schema.v1.0.json did (backend/tests/test_contracts.py proves this on edge cases), and every stricter or new rule applies only to "1.1" events. See contracts/API.md 'Evidence boundaries (v1.1)'.

source_record_id.description: Stable per sensor record. Cowrie: sha256 of the raw JSON line. Web: request uuid. Dedup key is (ingest namespace, sensor_id, source_record_id); the namespace is 'live' for live events and 'replay:<lab_run_id>' for replay events.

origin_record_id.description: 1.1 only. Replay: source_record_id of the original captured record this replay copies. Must be null or absent on live events.

event_type.description: bait_served is 1.1 only: the sensor's own result record shows it returned content containing honeytokens.

session_id.description: Sensor session reference. Cowrie: its session id. Web (1.1): a non-reusable reference derived by the decoy (for example a keyed digest of the session cookie with a per-run key), never the bearer cookie itself; null when the decoy has no session.

lab_run_id.description: Set once per run. A run has exactly one capture_mode: the first accepted event fixes it, and events with the other mode for that run are rejected. Use a 'replay-' prefix for replay runs by convention.

attributes_v1_0.description: Frozen copy of the 1.0 attribute rules (contracts/history/event.schema.v1.0.json). Do not tighten.

client_version.description: Client-claimed banner. A claim, not identity.

query_redacted.description: Query string with any honeytoken or password values replaced by <redacted>

honeytoken_id.description: A honeytoken PRESENTED by the client (login, query). Served bait uses honeytoken_ids.

sha256.description: Digest of the content named by digest_scope.

outcome.description: 1.0 values keep their meaning ('served' = emulated_success for a synthetic file).

policy_revision.description: blocked_request: revision of the policy snapshot that denied it (M2).

observation_kind.description: What the record observed. If absent the backend derives it from event_type (API.md).

request_id.description: Web: one id per HTTP request; every record about that request carries it.

honeytoken_ids.description: bait_served (and command_input with requested_asset_id): tokens contained in the asset. Ids only, never values.

issuance_id.description: bait_served: unique per serving. With a static credential several issuances carry the same token; the backend then keeps the attribution ambiguous.

issued_expires_at.description: bait_served: optional expiry; null = valid until the run ends.

evidence_basis.description: bait_served: what shows the content was actually returned. sensor_response = the decoy logged sending the response (web). session_output_log = the sensor's own recorded output stream for the session contains the bait (e.g. a Cowrie TTY log). A command alone is never enough; see requested_asset_id.

requested_asset_id.description: command_input: the adapter recognised a read of this registered bait asset (e.g. 'cat notes.txt'). A request, not proof the content was returned.

fixture_version.description: Version label of the synthetic asset, a string such as 'env@1'.

digest_scope.description: What sha256 covers. 'partial' digests must never be presented as whole-content proof.

input_features.description: M4. Sanitised, bounded description of client input (query, form or JSON body) without any raw value. Lets the backend classify body payloads without storing them.

field_names.description: Names only. Values are never included, sensitive or not.

indicators.description: Fixed vocabulary computed by the producer on decoded input. The backend owns the classification it derives from these.

truncated.description: True if feature extraction stopped at a limit.

processing.description: M4. How the producer handled the request body, so an absent feature is not mistaken for a clean request.

body_bytes.description: Bytes received (may exceed what was parsed).

body_consumed.description: True only if the whole body was read; a full digest is valid only then.
